stemMd: The student wants to emphasise an inconvenience that a tide mill's design creates for the people who buy its flour. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The restored tide mill at Cleave Point, Devon, grinds flour for two hours on each falling tide, while the pond behind its dam empties.

options.label: B
options.textMd: A tide mill grinds only while its pond empties, so its hours move about fifty minutes later each day and Cleave Point customers must check a tide table.

options.label: C
options.textMd: When the tide is at its highest, a gate closes the pond behind the dam, and as the sea falls away outside, water let out of the pond turns the wheel.

options.label: D
options.textMd: A tide mill, like the restored one at Cleave Point in Devon, is a watermill driven by the rise and fall of the tide rather than by a river's current.

explanationMd:
Two conditions are packed into this goal, and both have to be met. The sentence must name an inconvenience, and the people inconvenienced must be *the customers*, not the miller and not the mill.

The sentence ending with the tide table is the only option that mentions customers at all, and it reaches them through the design: the mill grinds only while the pond empties, that constraint drags the opening times almost an hour later each day, and the result is that buyers must check a tide table before setting out. Design, consequence, inconvenience, in that order.

Check by striking out any option that fails either condition. The definition and the description of the gate and wheel both explain how the mill works with no consequence attached, and the sentence about two hours of grinding reports what the Cleave Point mill does. Each uses accurate notes, and the Cleave Point mill appears in two of them, but none of the three names a person who is put out by anything, so none can emphasise an inconvenience.

distractorRationale.d: This is a definition, with the Cleave Point mill added as an example. It distinguishes a tide mill from a river mill but attaches no consequence to that difference, so nobody is inconvenienced in it.
distractorRationale.a: This reports the mill's output and grinding time. Two hours of grinding per falling tide, while the pond empties, is a fact about the mill's operation, not a difficulty stated from the customer's side.
distractorRationale.c: This describes the mechanism that drives the wheel: the gate closing at high tide and the pond draining as the sea falls. It is the cause of the inconvenience rather than the inconvenience, and it never reaches the people who buy the flour.

accessibilityText: Using the six student notes about tide mills, choose the sentence that best emphasises an inconvenience the tide mill's design creates for its flour customers. The four choices say: that the restored tide mill at Cleave Point, Devon, grinds flour for two hours on each falling tide, while the pond behind its dam empties; that a tide mill grinds only while its pond empties, so its hours move about fifty minutes later each day and Cleave Point customers must check a tide table; that when the tide is at its highest a gate closes the pond behind the dam, and as the sea falls away outside, water let out of the pond turns the wheel; and that a tide mill, like the restored one at Cleave Point, is a watermill driven by the rise and fall of the tide rather than by a river's current.

provenance.notes: Original item. The goal names a specific affected party, so the item turns on which sentence reaches the customers rather than on which is most informative.

review.author: digital-sat-wave4-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: The inconvenience for buyers is that opening hours shift about 50 minutes a day, so customers must check a tide table. B links that to the design, since the mill grinds only while the pond empties. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave7-sat-rw-run1) reached the same answer: The inconvenience is that the hours shift about fifty minutes later each day, so customers must consult a tide table. Only B links the design to that customer burden. A, C and D describe the operation or the definition.]

review.notes: Author's own solve and uniqueness check: Goal requires (i) an inconvenience and (ii) customers as the affected party. Only D mentions customers, and it links them to the design through the shifting hours. A and C are mechanism, B is output; none names anyone inconvenienced. Unique.
